reviews.title: Revised Review.
reviews.text:
The app started out great. I loved it. It was the first one of these apps that actually let me log my meals easily and fore free.
Then it stopped working.
It identified tomato soup as crackers.
It said “AKA” was a vulgar term and Apple Jelly was a reference to an adult website.
It removed all the ingredients from the meal, meaning I couldn’t edit the ingredients, and when I asked it to let
me, it signed me out or said I was jailbreaking the ai.
It says I’m out of meals when I’ve only logged three and clearly still have energy left.
Anytime I want to edit a meal, it just deletes the meal entirely.
Please fix this, I am very close to deleting this app, I have already been forced to lower my rating to three stars.

reviews.title: Love this App
reviews.text:
This is the first time ever I’ve been able to consistently log my meals. 

Statistically logging your food is shown to be one of the most effective tools for weight loss and management. 

I’ve lost 10 pounds after trying for years to drop weight! 

Amino makes it so easy with the snap feature. I often check its evaluation with Gemini and am pleased that they’re in agreement. 

Yes! I recommend this. And it’s free!! Although I did decide to purchase.

reviews.title: Weekly caloric tracker
reviews.text:
I have used this app over a couple of months and I am very fond of the features it has. However, the recent update added a paywall onto some of the basic features an app should have like telling your average intake over a week. I am unable to view that info, so I have switched to a different app simultaneously to track that. It is very upsetting to see everything good about the app behind a paywall. Please bring back some of the features.
My updated response: there still is not a weekly overview of the calorie intake because it is under the paid version of the app please provide insight on where to look if there is a free weekly intake tracker.

reviews.title: No longer fully free
reviews.text: One of the things that made me try this app earlier this year was that I could use the app for free by earning points. Before, you could take as many pictures of food as you wanted and get free AI analysis. In their bio they literally stated that they were proud that the app was free with no behind the scenes charges. Now you only get 5 free pics per day and the AI is slow and often times inaccurate. No longer like this app. And I no longer recommend it.

reviews.title: Amino: AI Calorie Tracker
reviews.text: Very user-friendly app. However it can’t tell if what you’re showing it is mixed in with anything else. My solution is (for example)is to put the tuna on one side of the plate, the scoop of mayo next to it, spot of mustard on same said plate, the bread, etc. This way the app sees all the ingredients not just the finish product. It will give you more accurate calorie count. You can mix all your ingredients later(after your photo has been taken) and eat. It’s an easy solution. I actually find this app cute and fun to use!
